title: Stack vs heap
hook: Your app uses two kinds of memory. Stack is for quick, short jobs. Heap is for things that need to last longer.

steps.caption: You call a function. The computer puts its short notes on the Stack — like a sticky note on a pile.

nodeCaptions.code: Your code calls a function (a small job).
nodeCaptions.stack: Stack = a neat pile. Newest note goes on top.

steps.caption: Sometimes you need a bigger thing that should stay after the function ends. That goes on the Heap.

nodeCaptions.code: You ask for space that can last longer.
nodeCaptions.heap: Heap = a big storage room. Things stay until you clean them up.

steps.caption: The function finishes. The Stack sticky note is thrown away. The Heap thing can still be there.

nodeCaptions.stack: Top note comes off. Those short notes are gone.
nodeCaptions.heap: Heap stuff does not vanish automatically — it waits until it is freed.

takeaways: Stack = short notes for a function. They go away when the function ends.
Heap = longer storage. You (or the language) must clean it up later.
Bugs like “memory leaks” usually mean Heap stuff was never cleaned up.

quiz.question: Where do a function’s short local notes usually live?
quiz.explanation: Short local values sit on the Stack and leave when the function ends.

quiz.question: What is the Heap good for?
choices: Data that needs to last longer than one function
quiz.explanation: Heap memory can stay after a function returns.

quiz.question: A function ends. What happens to its Stack sticky note?
choices: It becomes a file on Disk
quiz.explanation: When the function returns, its Stack frame (sticky note) is popped off.
